statement: The paper defines hidden bilinear games whose parameter vectors are separately mapped through smooth functions before entering a bilinear zero-sum payoff.
conditions: Separate smooth maps F and G
limits: Does not capture all GAN or MARL interactions

statement: Theorem 3 states that, for safe initial conditions in the two-strategy hidden bilinear system, the continuous-time GDA orbit is periodic.
limits: Not a statement about arbitrary nonconvex games or unsafe initializations

statement: Theorem 4 states that time averages of the mapped strategies and expected utility converge to their Nash-equilibrium values in the two-strategy safe-initialization setting.
conditions: Conditions of the two-strategy system and safe initialization
limits: Last iterates remain periodic; averaging is essential

statement: Theorems 6-7 connect higher-dimensional trajectories to Poincare recurrence, with Theorem 7 requiring sigmoid maps or the stated one-to-one safe-map condition.
conditions: Additional map conditions for full-flow recurrence

statement: Theorems 8 and 10 construct continuous- and discrete-time systems where a positive-measure set of initial conditions converges to fixed points that are not equilibria of the hidden game.
conditions: Selected learning rate for the discrete theorem
limits: Existence counterexample, not prevalence across all games

statement: The negative results are bounded to hidden bilinear zero-sum structure and cannot be cited as proof that every general-sum MARL optimizer cycles or converges spuriously.
Cycling, energy drift, and initialization-dependent fixed points are prospective diagnostics for HMASD optimizers with rotational components; candidate repairs require separate evidence.
conditions: Mechanism must exhibit a comparable vector field
